_comment: compiler-bench: per-engine incrementalizability survey over openivm's TPC-C query corpus.
A port of openivm's benchmark/src/rewriter_benchmark.cpp to every engine: instead of
timing one TPC-DI DAG, it pushes 2,505 queries at an engine and reports what fraction
its compiler can maintain incrementally.
With feature_flags.compiler_bench on, an experiment runs the survey INSTEAD of the
timed 3-batch benchmark - thousands of created/dropped views would otherwise pollute
timings. batch_*_pct are still required by the schema but unused.
Per query: run the SELECT -> CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW -> ask the engine whether it
will maintain it incrementally -> apply base-table deltas -> refresh -> verify the
view equals a re-run of the query. The phase a query stops at is its result.
DuckDB and DuckDB-OpenIVM run OpenIVM's source SQL directly. Only engines with a
different SQL dialect receive an LPTS-rendered equivalent. Target-rendering failures
are reported as translation_failed, never skipped. Cross-engine percentages are only
comparable over the common subset (summary.json -> common_subset).
compiler_bench.scale_factor is separate from the experiment's: incrementalizability
does not depend on data volume, so the survey stays small (3 warehouses).
Usage (host):
BENCHMARK_EXPERIMENTS_FILE=src/containers/benchmark-server/experiments/compiler-bench.json \
bash src/.scripts/benchmark.sh
Storage: the DuckDB-family engines can run the survey against plain DuckDB tables or
DuckLake (the storage the timed benchmark actually uses). The native corpus is
storage-agnostic - table names are unqualified - so the SAME queries run either way,
and all 2,505 queries get DuckLake coverage rather than only OpenIVM's hand-written
ducklake_* variants. Results land under results/<engine>-ducklake/ so the two runs do
not overwrite each other. OpenIVM can classify a query differently when the scan is a
DuckLake scan, which is the point of surveying both.
Artifacts:
mount/compiler-bench/corpus/<dialect>/            native/rendered queries + translation.csv
mount/compiler-bench/results/<engine>[-ducklake]/ results.csv + summary.json
